_about: Henry's law constants of gases in water at infinite dilution, mole-fraction based: p_i = H x_i (strictly f_i = H x_i), H in kPa. Equations and units per entry; see src/thermo/henry.js.

vapourPressure.form: ln(p1*/pc1) = (Tc1/T) sum_i a_i tau^b_i, tau = 1 - T/Tc1
vapourPressure.source: IAPWS G7-04 (2004), Guideline on the Henry's constant and vapor-liquid distribution constant for gases in H2O and D2O at high temperatures, eq. 4 and table 1 (the IAPWS saturation-pressure equation of Wagner and Pruss). Coefficients transcribed from the open-source iapws Python package 1.5.5 (iapws/_iapws.py, function _Henry), which implements the guideline and reproduces the guideline's check values (table 6) to all printed digits.

pairs.form: Hcp = exp(A + B/T + C ln T), mol/(m3 Pa); converted to H (kPa) = rho_w / (M_w Hcp) / 1000 with rho_w = 997 kg/m3 (the conversion used by the compilation)
pairs.source: R. Sander, Compilation of Henry's law constants (version 5.0.0) for water as solvent, Atmos. Chem. Phys. 23 (2023) 10901-12440, doi:10.5194/acp-23-10901-2023, open access CC BY 4.0, https://henrys-law.org/henry/casrn/74-85-1, note 309: three-parameter fit by Sander to the measurements of T. J. Morrison and F. Billett, J. Chem. Soc. (1952) 3819, doi:10.1039/JR9520003819.
pairs.validity: The compilation does not state the temperature range of the fit. Fugacity accepts 273.15-353.15 K, the range over which this fit and the two other measured data sets in the compilation (Maassen 1995, note 307; Reichl 1995, note 308) agree within 7.5 % (test/henry.test.js; largest difference 7.2 % at 273.15 K, Maassen 1995). Ethylene is not covered by IAPWS G7-04.
